title: Shared Expenses API
summary: Fix lost and invented cents in the expense splits of a flatmates-and-trips app, add balances, a deterministic settle-up plan and settlement payments, then keep them exact and fast on a group with 150,000 expenses.
overview:
You've joined **TallyUp**, an app for flatmates and travel groups who share costs. This codebase is its API: a group has members, anyone can record an expense they paid for and say how it is split (equally, by exact amounts, or by shares), and the app shows who is owed what and who should pay whom to settle up. Every group has one currency, and all money is integer cents.

It is an Express 4 app split the usual way: `src/routes/` maps URLs to `src/controllers/`, which read the request and pick the status code; `src/services/` hold the business rules (`money.js` works out each member's share of an expense); `src/store/memory-store.js` stands in for the database, with every call asynchronous like a real round trip. Errors are classes in `src/errors.js` that `src/middleware/error-handler.js` turns into JSON.

Start with `README.md`: it documents the money rules, every endpoint, status code and error shape, and it is the contract the tests check. Then follow `POST /api/groups/:groupId/expenses` from the router to the store. `demo.js` starts the app on a free port and records an expense in the sample flat group.

phases.title: The cents don't add up
phases.instructions:
Two reports came in this week:

> **Support:** *"A group of three split a 100.00 dinner. The app shows 33.33 for each of them, 99.99 in total, so a cent has vanished. Another group's 2.00 snack split three ways shows 0.67 each, 2.01 in total, and now that group's balances don't add up to zero. It only happens when the amount doesn't divide evenly."*

> **A user:** *"My flatmate entered exact amounts for a 100.00 bill: 40.00 and 40.00. The app accepted it and recorded the expense, but 20.00 of the bill is nobody's share. I can't even tell who should cover it."*

Find the root cause of each and fix them. The expected behaviour is in the **Money rules** section of `README.md`: the shares of an expense always add up to its amount exactly, leftover cents go one at a time to the members with the largest remainder (ties in ascending member id order), and an `exact` split must add up to `amountCents` or be rejected with `422`. Keep every other status code and error shape as it is.

**Done when:** all tests in `tests/phase1.test.js` pass.
hints: Reproduce first: post a 10000-cent equal split between three members with `node demo.js` or a quick request, and add up the `shares` in the response. Then do the same with an `exact` split whose amounts are too small.

Two files, one small change each. Shares come from `allocate` in `src/services/money.js`: what happens to the cents that don't divide evenly when every share is rounded on its own? Exact amounts are checked in `parseSplit` in `src/validation.js`: read the comparison against `amountCents` carefully.

Floor every share first, count how many cents are left, and hand them out one at a time in order of largest remainder `(totalCents * weight) % totalWeight`, earlier members first on ties. For the exact split, the sum must equal `amountCents`, not merely not exceed it.

phases.title: Balances and settling up
phases.instructions:
The app's home screen needs three things that don't exist yet. `GET .../balances` and `GET .../settle-up` currently answer with a 500, and nothing can record a payment between members. Build them across the layers: route, controller, service and store. Start from the stubs in `src/services/balance-service.js`; the routes and controllers for the two reads exist already, and settlements need new ones.

**Balances.** A member's balance is what they paid out, minus their shares of every expense, plus settlements they sent, minus settlements they received. Positive means the group owes them.

* `GET /api/groups/:groupId/balances` returns `200` with `{"groupId", "currency", "balances": [{"memberId", "name", "balanceCents"}]}`: every member of the group (including those with `0`), ascending by member id.
* `GET /api/groups/:groupId/balances/:memberId` returns one entry: `{"groupId", "currency", "memberId", "name", "balanceCents"}`.
* An unknown group, or a member who is not in that group, is `404` with `error.code` `not_found`.

**Settle up.** `GET /api/groups/:groupId/settle-up` returns `200` with `{"groupId", "currency", "transfers": [{"fromId", "toId", "amountCents"}]}`, a list of payments that bring every balance to zero. The rule is **greedy and deterministic**: repeat until nobody owes anything: take the member who owes the most (ties: lowest member id) and the member who is owed the most (ties: lowest member id); the first pays the second the smaller of the two amounts. Transfers are listed in the order they are produced; members with a zero balance never appear; a settled group has `"transfers": []`.

**Settlements.** `POST /api/groups/:groupId/settlements` with `{"fromId", "toId", "amountCents"}` records that one member paid another.

* Success is `201` with `Location: /api/groups/<groupId>/settlements/<id>` and `{"id", "groupId", "fromId", "toId", "amountCents", "currency", "createdAt"}` (ids look like `set_00001`). `GET /api/groups/:groupId/settlements/:settlementId` returns it again, or `404`.
* `fromId` and `toId` must be member ids, different from each other, and `amountCents` a whole number of at least 1: otherwise `422` with `{"error": {"code": "validation_error", "fields": {...}}}` naming **every** bad field (`fromId`, `toId`, `amountCents`). Malformed JSON is `400`.
* A member who is not in the group is `404`. Check order: group (404), body (422), members (404). Paying more than you owe is allowed; the balance just changes sign.

**Done when:** the phase 1 and phase 2 tests pass.
hints: Keep the layers. Parse the settlement body in `src/validation.js` (next to `parseExpenseInput`, throwing the same `ValidationError`), keep the rules in `balance-service.js`, add the two routes and two controller methods, and give the store a second collection next to expenses. The store already loads `expenses`; model `settlements` the same way.

Balances are a fold over history. Start every member of the group at 0, add `amountCents` to the payer and subtract each share's `cents` for every expense, then add settlements to `fromId` and subtract them from `toId`. The sum of all balances must be 0, which is a handy assertion while developing.

Settle-up: split the members into debtors (negative) and creditors (positive) with positive amounts. Loop: pick the largest of each with a comparator that falls back to the lower id, emit `min(debt, credit)`, subtract it from both, and drop whoever reached 0. Both lists empty at the same time because the balances sum to zero.

phases.title: The group with 150,000 expenses
phases.instructions:
Two production reports:

> **On-call:** *"The 'Everyone, since 2019' group has 150,000 expenses. The app reads its balances, two members' balances and the settle-up plan right after every new expense, and each of those requests now takes tens of milliseconds of pure CPU. A busy evening pins the server."*

> **Support:** *"During a big trip, with lots of people adding expenses and payments at once, one group's balances were briefly off by someone else's expense. They fixed themselves later, but nobody trusts the numbers now."*

Make the balance endpoints production-ready:

1. **Fast at any history size.** `GET /balances`, `GET /balances/:memberId` and `GET /settle-up` must not get slower as a group accumulates expenses and settlements. The tests seed one group with 150,000 expenses, then repeat 25 rounds of *post an expense, then read the group's balances, two members' balances and the settle-up plan together*, and require the whole loop to take **under 1.5 seconds**. Writing an expense stays O(participants).
2. **Always exact.** Balances must add up to zero at every moment, including when a read overlaps a write: an expense or settlement is reflected in balances completely or not at all. No update may be lost when many expenses and settlements are posted at the same time (the store has a few milliseconds of latency, so requests really overlap).
3. **Same behaviour.** Every response, status code and rule from phases 1 and 2 stays as it is. Note that tests create the store with `createStore({groups, expenses, settlements})`, so the store must cope with history it is handed at start-up, not just with writes made through the API.

**Done when:** all three phases' tests pass.
hints: Look at what one `GET /balances` does in the service: how many expenses does it touch, and how many of them were already counted by the previous request? Write a number on it: 150,000 expenses times about 7 shares each, three or four times per new expense.

A balance is a running total, so keep one per member per group and update it when the data is written instead of recomputing it when the data is read. The best place is the store, in the same synchronous step that appends the expense or settlement: with no `await` between the append and the ledger update, no reader can ever see one without the other, and two concurrent writers cannot interleave a read-modify-write.

Add a ledger (a `Map` of group id to a `Map` of member id to cents) to the store. Update it from `addExpense` and `addSettlement`, which the constructor also calls for the history it is handed, and expose `getBalances(groupId)` returning a copy. The service then builds its response from the ledger and the group's member list (members missing from the ledger are `0`) and never calls `listExpenses` again.

debrief: How did you confirm each of the two money bugs before changing code? Explain why rounding every share separately loses or creates cents, and why the leftover cents go to the largest remainder, with ties in member id order, rather than to the payer or to one fixed member.

Walk through how you built balances and the greedy settle-up. Why is the order of balances and transfers deterministic, how many transfers can there be at most, and does greedy always give the fewest possible payments? What would change for a group of thousands of members?

Explain why recomputing balances from the history stopped scaling and how the running ledger fixes it. Where does it have to be updated so that reads never see half a write or lose an update, and how did you check that the AI-generated code was actually correct and not just fast on the happy path?
